issues.note: The front asks which four keys a `SKILL.md` "can carry", which asserts a closed set. Domain-3_v2 §3.3 heads that table "### SKILL.md Frontmatter Options" and lists four options — it never says only four keys exist. A learner who memorizes an exhaustive four-key list will read a fifth key in a stem as a fabricated distractor. Reword to the corpus's own framing. Secondary: the key is `context`; `fork` is its value.

issues.note: Primary cite is wrong. The claim (which work forks, which stays in the main session) lives in Key-Distinctions_v1 #13, whose 'Use for' row reads: "Discovery, analysis, exploration, brainstorming | Implementation, design, conversation". Domain-3_v2 §3.3 is cited first but never enumerates those categories — it only gives two exam scenarios (`/analyze-codebase`, `/explore-alternatives`). CARD-SPEC §6: "The primary cite comes first, and it must be the section the back's claim is actually drawn from."

Same question as d3-004 in different words. d3-004 front: "Which config location carries a standard to everyone who clones the repository, and which keeps it on one machine?" d3-064 front: "Which CLAUDE.md location travels with the repository to every teammate, and which one stays on one machine?" Identical retrieval, identical answer. CARD-SPEC §10: "Do not write two cards that ask the same thing in different words." Keep d3-004; if the trap line on d3-064 is worth saving, move it onto d3-004.

Duplicate of d3-025. d3-025 front: "A personal skill and a project skill both define `/commit`. Which definition runs?" d3-067 front: "A personal skill and a project skill share the name `commit`. Which one runs?" The backs are word-for-word the same claim: "The personal one at `~/.claude/skills/commit/SKILL.md` overrides the project skill of the same name." Keep d3-025 (its trap names the documented ❌ from Domain-3_v2 §3.5, the `/my-commit` rename).

Duplicate of d3-042. Backs are identical apart from punctuation: d3-042 "`-p` (or `--print`): it processes the prompt, prints the result to stdout, and exits" vs d3-070 "`-p` (or `--print`) -- it processes the prompt, prints the result to stdout, and exits", and both traps name `CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true` and `--batch`. d3-043 already covers the hang framing ("What becomes of a CI job that calls `claude` with a prompt and leaves off `-p`?"). Killing this still leaves 11 `d3.6` cards, well over the ≥7 minimum in CARD-SPEC §7.

Same answer, same source section as d3-052: "`--output-format json` plus `--json-schema`". d3-052 is the corpus's own exam scenario (Domain-3_v2 §3.9: "Team wants to auto-post each finding as an inline GitHub PR comment") and its trap already carries the CLAUDE.md-Output-Format and prompt-instruction distractors that d3-072 repeats. Keep d3-052; d3-053 separately covers the schema-vs-format distinction.

Duplicate of d3-046 — the backs are character-identical: "The previous run's findings, with an instruction to report only new or still-unaddressed issues." The fronts describe the same corpus scenario (Domain-3_v2 §3.8: "CI review posts near-duplicate comments (with slightly different wording) every time the author pushes a follow-up commit"), and both traps state the same blank-slate misconception. Keep d3-046.

Same fact as d3-048. d3-048 front: "How does a CI-invoked Claude Code learn the project's testing standards, fixture conventions, and review criteria?" d3-074 asks the same thing with a fixture-convention wrapper and answers with the same CLAUDE.md claim drawn from the same bullet in Domain-3_v2 §3.8: "CLAUDE.md is the mechanism for giving CI-invoked Claude project context: testing standards, fixture conventions, review criteria".

The trap invents a distractor the corpus does not document for this scenario: "`max_tokens` governs length rather than adherence". `max_tokens` appears nowhere in Domain-3_v2 §3.8, and it is a Messages API parameter, not a Claude Code CI knob. CARD-SPEC §10: "Do not invent flags, parameters, or behaviors. If the corpus does not say it, it does not go on a card." If this card is kept instead of d3-048, that clause must be deleted.

Bundles two facts already drilled individually: d3-006 ("`@` immediately before the path with no space ... relative paths resolve against the file holding the import") and d3-005 ("Five levels."). Both trace to the same three bullets in Domain-3_v2 §3.1 ("Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import"; "Maximum import nesting depth is 5"). Third card on the same two facts; keep d3-005 and d3-006.

Back is identical to d3-028's: "Large scope, architectural decisions, several viable approaches, and changes spanning many files." Its trap (reactive switching) is already a card of its own, d3-029, drawn from the same line in Domain-3_v2 §3.6 ("Exam trap: 'Start in direct execution and switch to planning when it gets hard' → Wrong"). Keep d3-028 and d3-029.

Duplicate of d3-037 — same corpus scenario (Domain-3_v2 §3.7.2: "Migration script mishandles null values; the developer keeps describing the bug in prose") and the same back: d3-037 "a sample input row containing nulls plus the exact expected output, iterated until that test passes" vs d3-077 "a sample input row containing nulls plus the exact expected output -- iterated until it passes". Exact duplicate of d3-060 — identical `front`, identical `back`, identical single cite `Domain-3_v2 §3.12`. One of the two must go; the content itself is correct against §3.12 ("`--resume` | Resume a previous (named) Claude Code session with saved context"; "`fork_session` | ... both forks inherit context up to the branch point, then diverge").

Same corpus scenario and same answer as d3-003, which already states the fix in its back ("Moving it to the project-level config fixes it"). Both trace to Domain-3_v2 §3.1: "Root cause: ✅ Guidance is in the original developers' `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` ... Fix: Move instruction to project-level config". d3-079's front just states d3-003's answer and asks for the second half. Keep d3-003.

Overlaps d3-008 heavily. The two traps are the same sentence rewritten — d3-008: "restating the instruction more forcefully every session treats the symptom and leaves the discovery problem in place"; d3-080: "restating the rule more forcefully each session treats the symptom of a file that was never discovered" — both drawn from the single ❌ bullet in Domain-3_v2 §3.1 ("Repeat the instruction louder in the prompt each session (treats symptom, not root cause)"). The card survives only as the definitional 'what does `/memory` output' half; drop its trap so it is not a reworded copy of d3-008's.
